newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian exodus to Italy continues unabated.
newsitem.headline: Albanian exodus to Italy continues unabated.

text.p: An Albanian military helicopter landed in southern Italy with 33 refugees on board on Saturday while scores more docked on rusty merchant ships and fishing boats fleeing across the Adriatic.
The police headquarters in the southeast Italian port of Brindisi said that by 1000 GMT, 961 Albanians had arrived there and were being assisted by authorities.
They said 83 were deserting soldiers or sailors and were being held at a naval base before a planned transfer to a gymnasium in the city.

Italian coastguards in Rome said a convoy of 20 to 30 vessels, which had earlier stretched out for about 15 miles across the Adriatic Sea, arrived as the exodus from anarchy in the Balkan state continued unabated.
Another fishing boat with an estimated 100 people on board, whom Italian news agencies said were believed to be sick hospital patients, was intercepted off Brindisi.
Officials in the port of Bari further north said they were sheltering 204 Albanians in various centres.
Brindisi police chief Antonio Ruggiero told reporters the situation there was "absolutely under control" although the port was completely full after the latest arrivals.
The Albanians have crossed the Adriatic on a range of vessels, from ancient and decrepit navy patrol boats to small fishing boats and larger freighters.
Others have fled by helicopter. Police said the one that arrived on Saturday at a site owned by helicopter makers Agusta had five children and six soldiers among the passengers.
"The police are doing their best to ensure that the presence of the Albanians is not noticed by the local population, and certainly not as a problem," Ruggiero said.
He added that police had for several days been asking the Red Cross and local social services to provide nappies and baby care products as well as food for the Albanians.
About half of the 90 refugees on board two fishing boats that entered the small harbour at Savelletri, near Brindisi, on Saturday were children, mostly under the age of 10.
One of the boats had broken down and the other had towed it for much of the journey across the Adriatic.

Italy, a magnet for Albanian illegal immigrants, has sought to discourage refugees since protests sparked by the collapse of shady saving schemes erupted this month into armed insurrection in southern Albania. Unrest has now spread across the country.
At least 17 Albanian navy vessels, most of them small patrol boats built decades ago by the Chinese, limped into southern Italian ports under escort on Friday.
The exodus has raised fears in Italy of a repeat of the tide of 40,000 Albanians who flocked to southeast ports on an armada of ships in 1991 after Stalinist rule crumbled in Europe's poorest state.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said on Friday it had urged Italy and Albania's neighbour Greece to allow Albanians fleeing this month's turmoil to enter and stay "as long as necessary".
